subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Reputation and Markets
description: A micro-lesson that makes Reputation and Markets usable.

hook.text: eBay sellers with 99% ratings get 8% higher prices than identical sellers with 97% ratings.

buildup.text: Reputation solves the trust problem in anonymous markets. Without it, strangers cannot trade safely online.

discovery.text: Reputation systems turn repeated interactions into a public record. Good behavior is rewarded; bad behavior is punished.

twist.text: Gaming reputation is big business. Fake reviews, bought ratings, and review bombing threaten the system's credibility.

climax.text: Digital reputation is the new currency of trust. Protecting its integrity is essential for online marketplaces.

punchline.text: In online markets, your reputation is your price tag.

quiz.question: Why do reputation systems matter in online markets?
options: They make products look more expensive
They solve the trust problem between anonymous strangers
They are required by law for all sellers

details.summary: Reputation serves as an informal enforcement mechanism in markets where formal contracts are incomplete. Businesses and individuals invest heavily in reputation because it enables trust-based transactions that would otherwise be too risky without legal guarantees.
details.whyItMatters: Online markets like eBay and Airbnb function primarily because of reputation systems. Without seller ratings and reviews, the information asymmetry between buyers and sellers would make most transactions too risky to complete.
takeaways: Reputation substitutes for formal contracts in enabling trust-based trade
Online reputation systems made large-scale stranger-to-stranger commerce viable
Reputation is a valuable economic asset that commands price premiums

faq.question: How do reputation systems solve the trust problem?
faq.answer: Ratings and reviews create a public record of past behavior. Sellers who cheat lose reputation and future business. The threat of reputation damage incentivizes honest behavior, making transactions possible between strangers who will never interact again.

faq.question: Can reputation systems be manipulated?
faq.answer: Yes, through fake reviews, retaliation ratings, and strategic forgiveness. Platforms combat manipulation with verified purchase requirements, detection algorithms, and weighting recent reviews more heavily. But no system is immune to gaming.
